name: Ropes

pages.text: Rope can be strung up to climb down cliffs and shafts. Use it on the tip of a $(thing)Rock Spike$() or on a $(thing)Metal Rope Anchor$() with $(item)$(k:key.use)$() to tie it off; the block then becomes an anchor.

Using $(item)$(k:key.use)$() on the rope again throws it out in the direction you are facing, laying down a rope you can climb. To recall the rope, use an empty hand on the anchor with $(item)$(k:key.use)$(): the rope is returned to you piece by piece, and the spike turns back into an anchor.

pages.title: Rope Anchors
pages.text: $(thing)Rock Spikes$() cannot be picked up, so a $(thing)Metal Rope Anchor$() can be used wherever an anchor is needed. Apart from steel, every metal that has $(thing)Rods$() can be made into one.$(br2)Craft one from two $(thing)Rods$() of that metal and one $(thing)Glue$().

pages.title: Reinforcing An Anchor
pages.text: A freshly placed $(thing)Metal Rope Anchor$() is not secured yet: it takes up two blocks of height and no rope can be tied to it. Strike it with any $(thing)Hammer$() using $(item)$(k:key.use)$(); every strike drives it deeper, and after three strikes it is secured, drops to a single block, and a rope can be tied to it.
